eventMetadata.context_description:
**Short-term forecast uncertainty around the seasonal average drives the tight clustering of implied probabilities near 32–34°C for Kuala Lumpur’s July 31 daily maximum.** 

Kuala Lumpur’s southwest monsoon climatology typically produces afternoon highs of 31–33°C, with the urban heat island and high humidity pushing readings toward the upper end on clearer days. Recent model guidance and the July 27 outcome of exactly 33°C illustrate how modest differences in morning cloud cover, timing of convective showers, or boundary-layer mixing can shift the peak by 1–2°C. Strengthening El Niño conditions have raised the regional temperature baseline and reduced rainfall likelihood, tilting the distribution slightly above the long-term July mean of ~33°C, yet the market’s near-even split between 33°C (29.5%) and 34°C (27.5%) reflects residual uncertainty in the final 48-hour convective evolution. Official short-range updates from MetMalaysia and global ensembles will determine whether the peak settles in the lower or upper half of the narrow 32–34°C window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent high-pressure ridging over the western Mediterranean, reinforced by subtropical and African anticyclone influences, continues to advect hot, dry air northward into northern Italy, sustaining elevated temperatures across the Po Valley through the end of July.** 

Clear skies, light winds, and strong daytime insolation are maximizing surface heating, while Milan’s urban heat island effect adds several degrees relative to surrounding rural areas. Recent ensemble guidance from leading models (ECMWF and GFS) shows maximum temperatures clustering in the mid-to-upper 30s °C on July 31, with limited spread that keeps 36 °C and 37 °C as the two most probable outcomes and explains their near-equal market shares. 

Earlier 2026 European heat episodes have already produced multiple red alerts for Milan and confirmed peaks above 35 °C, providing historical context for the current setup. The market’s tight distribution around these values reflects remaining uncertainty in exact peak timing and any minor model adjustments before the official daily maximum (typically measured at Milano Linate or Malpensa stations) is recorded on July 31.

**Recent model consensus from sources like the BBC and European forecasts points to a peak high near 38°C in Madrid on July 31, 2026, under persistent high-pressure dominance, clear skies, and light southwesterly winds that maximize daytime solar heating while limiting cloud cover or cooling.** 

This aligns with the market-implied odds favoring 38°C (47%) over 37°C (28.5%) or 39°C (25%), reflecting tight spreads driven by ensemble variability in exact maximum timing and urban heat-island effects at official stations. Madrid has already recorded daily highs of 38°C in recent days amid a broader Iberian heatwave, with July climatology showing typical maxima around 32–34°C but current conditions pushing 3–6°C above average. 

Key resolution factors include the official maximum reported by AEMET or equivalent monitoring, with minimal precipitation expected to keep temperatures elevated; updated runs from GFS and ECMWF in the next 24–48 hours could narrow the 37–39°C window as landfall timing and steering patterns clarify. Traders appear to weigh the strong consensus for peak heat against realistic model divergence typical this close to the event.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 1 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

This market can not resolve until data for this date has been published.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent passage of Typhoon Noul, which brought heavy rain and strong winds to Hong Kong around July 26, has left residual cloud cover and moisture that may moderate maximum temperatures on August 1. Official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory point to typical late-summer conditions dominated by the subtropical ridge, with high humidity supporting afternoon convective showers that can cap daytime heating. Historical climatology shows August daily maxima averaging near 31 °C, yet inter-day variability from cloud fraction, wind direction, and boundary-layer moisture often produces outcomes clustered between 27–29 °C. Traders appear to weigh these near-term meteorological uncertainties—particularly the timing and extent of any post-storm stabilization—resulting in closely matched implied probabilities across the 27 °C, 28 °C, and 29 °C bins. Updated model runs and observatory guidance expected in the next 48 hours will likely refine the range.
